title.narrative: ROAP/PAK03/Facilitating the flood affected population to access and protect their Housing, Land and Property Rights (HLP) to ensure tenure security through Capacity Building of the Key Stakeholders in the flood-affected districts of Pakistan

description.narrative:
The land registration/documentation system in Pakistan is complex and varies in urban and rural areas, leading to further complications. Customary practices and attitudes often deprive women of their rightful share in property and inheritance. Additionally, population growth has placed pressure on the already inadequate land registration system. Finding suitable housing parcels and resolving conflicts related to boundaries and ownership are significant challenges in post-flood rehabilitation.
To address these issues, there is a need for humanitarian assistance and a protection program that focuses on providing information and legal services to displaced and affected persons, especially those at risk of exclusion such as women, ensuring their access to land and property rights. The specific objective of UN-Habitat is to overcome legal obstacles, contribute to the recognition of legal status and access to rights and services, and improve access to justice through the provision of legal assistance. Enhancing the technical capacity of the Land Administration Authorities, particularly the Provincial Board of Revenue, is crucial to address grievances of affected persons after disasters.
The rationale behind providing information and legal assistance is to empower persons in situations of marginalization to make informed decisions regarding their well-being and durable solutions. Comprehensive information is necessary to understand the socio-economic and security conditions in return or resettlement areas. The UN-Habitat approach involves capacity building of local stakeholders and service-providing agencies, such as the Provincial Board of Revenue, through training sessions on Housing, Land, and Property Rights (HLP) and Information, Communication, and Legal Assistance. The goal is to protect HLP rights of flood-affected populations, especially vulnerable communities including women/girls, older persons, Persons with Disabilities, ethinic minorities and persons with sexual orientations (transgender); and strengthen the institutional capacities of the Provincial Board of Revenue to effectively address post-disaster HLP-related issues and resolve disputes. The intervention has the potential to become a regular program in the future.
